spots.bio: Pedestrian shopping mall in the city centre, with the Mall's Balls sculpture.
spots.name: Rundle Mall

spots.bio: Riverbank park with an 1882 rotunda, lake walking tracks and paddleboat hire.
spots.name: Torrens Lake and Elder Park
spots.note: Experience Adelaide (City of Adelaide visitor site) names Elder Park with the 1882 rotunda, lake walking tracks and paddleboat hire; SATC lists the riverbank and Popeye landing. Permanent, free. Popeye cruises are the operator, not the spot.

spots.bio: Free Japanese garden in the south Park Lands, with a teahouse and stepping stones.
spots.name: Adelaide Himeji Garden
spots.note: Experience Adelaide features the free Japanese garden (rock-and-sand and lake gardens, teahouse, stepping stones) in the south Park Lands, open daily. Case against: small, ~30 min.

spots.bio: Formal garden in the south Park Lands with a serpentine canal and statues.
spots.name: Veale Gardens
spots.note: Experience Adelaide lists Veale Gardens: formal serpentine canal, statues and the adjacent Adelaide-Qingdao Rose Garden, with guided walks on SATC. Permanent, free. Case against: ordinary Park Lands garden.

spots.bio: Conservation reserve protecting an intact dune system on the Adelaide coast, with a walk.
spots.name: Tennyson Dunes
spots.note: Wikivoyage and the parks agency name it as the state's most accessible intact dune system, with a walk to do (rule 1, 2).

spots.bio: Beach suburb north of Semaphore with an 1882 jetty, kiosk, playground and foreshore walk.
spots.name: Largs Bay
spots.note: City of Port Adelaide Enfield's visitor pages list the Largs Bay foreshore: 1882 jetty, kiosk, playground, walking paths, Largs Pier Hotel. A named beach and historic jetty. Council page was blocked to scripts (403); details from search. Against: no SATC listing.

spots.bio: Southern beach suburb with a jetty, esplanade and the Brighton Jetty Sculptures.
spots.name: Brighton
spots.note: SATC's Adelaide beaches guide features Brighton: jetty, esplanade, Brighton Jetty Sculptures; Wikivoyage names the beach via the Seaford line. A second-tier beach.

spots.bio: Family beach near the airport on Adelaide's western coast.
spots.name: West Beach

spots.bio: Coastal park with a glacial pavement, the Sugarloaf and a boardwalk, beside a swimming beach.
spots.name: Hallett Cove Conservation Park

spots.bio: Seaside suburb with a long jetty and a reef sanctuary with an 800 m underwater snorkel trail.
spots.name: Port Noarlunga
spots.note: SATC lists Port Noarlunga Beach, Jetty, Reef and Aquatic Trail and its beaches guide singles out the reef as some of the best snorkelling in SA; jetty with stairs to the reef.

spots.bio: Free, accessible 1.1 km coastal boardwalk under the Witton Bluff cliffs.
spots.name: Witton Bluff Base Trail
spots.note: southaustralia.com attraction page and Fleurieu tourism listing: 1.1 km free, accessible coastal boardwalk under Witton Bluff linking Port Noarlunga and Christies Beach (about 30 min one way), opened 2025. Objection: short, new; reached from the Port Noarlunga jetty area.

spots.bio: Clifftop coastal park with walking trails and views over Brighton, Glenelg and Marino Rocks Lighthouse.
spots.name: Marino Conservation Park
spots.note: NPWS SA and SATC list the park: walking trail with views over Brighton, Glenelg and Marino Rocks Lighthouse, the last coastal heath on the Adelaide coast (Botanical Trail ~1.2 km).
